entities.summary: Yevdokiya Yakovlevna Rachkevich was the deputy regimental commander and commissar of the 46th Guards Night Bomber Aviation Regiment during the Second World War. After the end of the war, Rachkevich traced the regiment's path throughout the war and managed to locate the remains of women in the regiment that were listed as missing in action so that they could receive a proper burial. Soldiers that went missing in action were considered potential traitors until their remains were found because they could have been captured, and Soviet prisoners of war were considered "guilty until proven innocent" of collaboration with the Axis, especially after Order No.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Rachkevich's efforts to locate and bury missing regiment members helped to rehabilitate the reputations of Soviet soldiers who were considered potential traitors after being captured by the Nazis. Her actions led to a shift in how the Soviet Union treated its prisoners of war, with an increase in successful repatriation and rehabilitation.
